variants.cost: Per iteration: two joint gradient-pair evaluations, equivalently four separately charged partial-gradient evaluations if those are distinct Oracle calls; two P_Q and two P_S projections, equivalently two product-set projections. Also vector arithmetic linear in n+m. Projection computation and gradient computation are separate resources; no unit-cost projection implementation or finite epsilon complexity is supplied.

public_inputs: Closed convex nonempty Q subset R^n and S subset R^m; differentiable phi; exact partial-gradient and projection access
Fixed alpha>0; printed Theorem 1 uses a block bound L>0 and 0<alpha<1/L
variants.query_and_update: At z_k=(x_k,y_k), evaluate g_x=phi_x(z_k), g_y=phi_y(z_k). Set xbar_k=P_Q(x_k-alpha*g_x), ybar_k=P_S(y_k+alpha*g_y). Evaluate h_x=phi_x(xbar_k,ybar_k), h_y=phi_y(xbar_k,ybar_k). Set x_{k+1}=P_Q(x_k-alpha*h_x), y_{k+1}=P_S(y_k+alpha*h_y). Both final projections start from z_k, not from the trial point.
variants.requirements: For executing the recurrence: exact partial gradients at feasible points and exact Euclidean P_Q,P_S. The printed performance setting additionally assumes phi convex in x, concave in y, both displayed block-gradient L bounds, and a nonempty saddle set; the constant inference in the printed proof remains restricted.
variants.state_and_initialization: Choose feasible (x_0,y_0) in Q×S and retain both coordinates as the base point of each iteration. Feasible initialization is the explicit convention of this record; Eq.(2) itself does not supply a separate initialization paragraph.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Eq.(2) is defined for alpha>0. Theorem 1 prints 0<alpha<1/L using its displayed block-gradient L; do not treat this as a verified universal convergence interval. No finite accuracy stopping rule is given in the inspected statement/proof. For a finite run, choose an external iteration budget K; this adds no accuracy guarantee.
